reps.name: Andrew Alonso
reps.headlineGap: A seventy-two-minute visit to a household planning to stay forever, and no replacement route was ever put on the table.
focus: Week 1: Offer the number — Every evaluation ends with a no-cost replacement figure offered out loud, whatever the repair is. Proof: An advisor offer on every recording.
Week 2: Use the forever-home answer — When a customer says they are staying, that sentence gets quoted back inside the presentation. Proof: The customer's own words in the option framing.
Week 3: Collect the fifth star — The review ask becomes the last item before the ladder goes in the van. Proof: Review asked on every call.

reps.name: Andrew Trujillo
reps.headlineGap: He asks the three questions almost nobody else asks, and there is no recording of what he did with the answers.
focus: Week 1: Record to the end — Recorder confirmed at the door and checked before leaving; a manager spot-checks that the last minute of tape is a goodbye, not a work interruption. Proof: Every recording reaches the end of the visit.
Week 2: Say the bill back — The monthly figure the customer gives is repeated inside the options. Proof: The customer's own number in the presentation.
Week 3: Ask for the review — Review ask added at the door on every call. Proof: Review asked on every recording.

reps.name: Benjamin Wyllie
reps.headlineGap: He seeds a five-star experience on every visit and has now gone the entire regrade period without collecting one.
focus: Week 1: Collect the star — Review asked before the signature screen, on every visit. Proof: Review asked on every recording.

Week 2: Number alongside every repair — Any customer who asks for a repair also leaves with a free replacement figure offered. Proof: An advisor offer on every call, including repair-preference calls.
Week 3: The bill question — Power bill asked in the first ten minutes on every call. Proof: The customer's own figure on every recording.

reps.name: Brandon Moreno
reps.headlineGap: The customer asked what the numbers look like and was told it varies, twice, with no advisor booked.
focus: Week 1: Book, don't describe — Every specialist mention ends with a proposed day and time. Proof: A date offered on every call.
Week 2: Approval promise restored — The approval line returns to the welcome on every visit. Proof: Present on every recording.
Week 3: Bill and recorder — Power bill asked in the first ten minutes; recorder verified before the van door closes. Proof: Customer's figure captured and the tape reaching the goodbye.

reps.name: Cole Pantol
reps.headlineGap: He runs the best-structured visit here and still has not asked a single customer for a review.
focus: Week 1: Ask for the star — Review ask becomes the last item before the ladder goes in the van. Proof: Review asked on every recording.
Week 2: The bill question — Power bill asked in the first ten minutes on every call. Proof: The customer's own figure on every recording.
Week 3: Record everything — Recorder confirmed at the door on every visit, not just the long ones. Proof: A recording for every job on the board.

reps.name: David Canales
reps.headlineGap: A customer said he would get other quotes, and the specialist option was dropped instead of being the reason to stay.
focus: Week 1: Answer the shopping signal — Any mention of other quotes is met with a proposed date for ours. Proof: A date offered every time a competitor is named.
Week 2: Three questions in the welcome — Goal, monthly bill and stay-length asked before the tools come out. Proof: All three on every recording.
Week 3: Offer, then comfort — Any interim-comfort advice comes after the offer, never instead of it. Proof: An advisor offer on every no-cool call.

reps.name: Francisco Valencia
reps.headlineGap: His best conversion of the day exists in ServiceTitan and nowhere else — the recording captured almost nothing.
focus: Week 1: Record the short calls — Recorder confirmed at the door on every job, however brief. Proof: A usable recording for every job on the board.
Week 2: The bill question — Power bill asked in the first ten minutes on every call. Proof: The customer's own figure on every recording.
Week 3: Ask for the star — Review asked before the signature screen on every visit. Proof: Review asked on every recording.

reps.name: Joe Mendoza
reps.headlineGap: He priced the ductwork by the run before he knew what the household could spend, and the conversation became arithmetic.
focus: Week 1: Budget before price — On any staged or large-ticket job, the spend question comes before the figure. Proof: A budget question on every multi-item presentation.
Week 2: Ask for the review — Review asked on every visit, especially the ones customers enjoy. Proof: Review asked on every recording.
Week 3: Two questions in the welcome — Goal and monthly bill asked before the tools come out. Proof: Both on every recording.

reps.name: Juan Tlatenchi
reps.headlineGap: He explained financing and offered a price appointment, then let a call-you-Sunday close the visit.
focus: Week 1: Book, don't offer — Every specialist mention ends with a date on the calendar and an easy way to cancel. Proof: An appointment set on every call where replacement is discussed.
Week 2: Record the whole visit — Recorder confirmed at the door and checked before the van door closes. Proof: A recording that starts with the greeting and ends with the goodbye.
Week 3: The welcome, said aloud — Approval promise, five-star framing and the goal question, in the first two minutes. Proof: All three audible on every recording.

reps.name: Mario Castro
reps.headlineGap: He is one of the higher-converting reps in this regrade period and nobody has ever heard him close.
focus: Week 1: Customer time only — Recorder captures the customer visit end to end and nothing after it. Proof: No technician-to-technician conversation on any recording.
Week 2: Capture one close — A manager rides along and one full presentation is recorded. Proof: One complete visit on tape this week.
Week 3: Bill question restored — Power bill asked in the welcome on every call. Proof: The customer's own figure on every recording.

reps.name: Nathan Colquitt
reps.headlineGap: Six graded days, and there is still no recording of Nathan reaching the end of a visit.
focus: Week 1: Record to the goodbye — Recorder confirmed at the door and verified before the van door closes; last minute spot-checked daily. Proof: Every recording ends with a goodbye, not a test.
Week 2: Three faults, one offer — Any call with multiple failures ends with a free replacement figure offered. Proof: An advisor offer on every multi-fault call.
Week 3: Keep the bill question — Power bill asked on every call and quoted back in the options. Proof: The customer's figure asked and repeated.

reps.name: Nikko April
reps.headlineGap: The customer said she did not know how long they would be in the house, and that answer was never picked up.
focus: Week 1: Rule out, then offer — Any repair he judges uneconomic is followed immediately by a free replacement figure. Proof: An advisor offer on every uneconomic-repair call.
Week 2: Chase the stay-length signal — Any mention of how long the household will be there gets a follow-up question and shapes the recommendation. Proof: The answer quoted in the options.
Week 3: Turn questions into visits — Every specialist consultation becomes a specialist appointment. Proof: A date offered whenever a specialist is mentioned.

reps.name: Robert Silinzy
reps.headlineGap: A customer handed him a hundred-dollar monthly increase and he offered a choice of directions rather than a date.
focus: Week 1: Use the bill figure — Every bill answer gets repeated inside the options as the cost of doing nothing. Proof: The customer's own figure in the presentation.

Week 2: Answer the price question with a date — Any question about replacement cost is answered by booking the person who can answer it. Proof: An appointment offered every time replacement is raised.
Week 3: Record to the end — Recorder confirmed at the door and verified before the van door closes. Proof: Every recording reaches the goodbye.
